title: Smart Look At The Week Ahead: RBI, Salesforce, Docusign And Macy’s
article:
Only one major central bank is set to announce interest rates next week. The Reserve Bank of India is expected to raise the repo rate from 5.5% to 5.75%. A rise in energy prices has pushed the inflation rate above the bank’s target band of 2% and 6%.
The RBI doesn’t need to wait for the Fed to move first. A rate hike by the US central bank in December is a nailed-on certainty. Additionally, with India’s economic growth expected to be robust, the RBI has enough leeway to move.
Aside from economic issues, Jensen Huang, who was reinstated as CEO of NVIDIA, will testify before Congress. He is expected to answer questions about the company’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed and NVIDIA’s business in China.
On the corporate front
Salesforce
(NYSE: CRM) does not believe that AI will disrupt its business. In fact, it is engaging AI to strengthen its business. It will integrate Anthropic’s Claude AI models into its products such as Slack and Agentforce. Salesforce could report high single-digit growth in revenue for the third quarter.
Docusign
(Nasdaq: DOCU) has also  embraced AI to improve customer experience. Its AI assistant can analyse agreement terms, reviews and generate contracts. The E-signature platform is expected to report a strong increase in earnings per share.
Macy’s
(NYSE: M) is nearing the end of a turnaround strategy to revitalise its store locations. The market will be looking to see if the department store can continue. In the second quarter, Macy’s said that growth has been driven by its reimagined stores. At that time, it raised its full-year guidance for both revenue and earnings per share.
Ulta Beauty
(Nasdaq: ULTA) is expected to announce another set of strong number for the quarter. Earnings could be almost 10% higher, whilst revenue could be up by 5%. The beauty-shop chain has invested in customer loyalty by personalising its promotional strategies. It has also continued to invest in mobile-app engagement and social media to fuel E-commerce growth.
